My recollection, however, I mean if it's going to cut to the chase, is that we addressed that before ourselves as May 12, 1993, and I think that was -- it's not only in the document itself but it's on the record at least once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It was the document you misread the date. It's Exhibit P6092, 12 of May, 19 -- let us see the date. Last page, probably. So 12th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So 51 weeks after the report submitted by Hrsum. I just wanted to establish that, that it was a year later and not before, as Mr. Tieger suggested in his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The dates speak for themselves. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Hrsum. On behalf of the Chamber, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is the next witness ready to come in?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then let's continue. While we are waiting for the next witness, going back to the issue I raised with respect to the witness from Portugal, I think we can file it publicly with a confidential annex. Did you -- could you explore the possibility and get confirmation from -- from the embassy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: If I was asked, I would suggest to start fresh tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wanted to conclude two witnesses by tomorrow just in case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: We can do it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You never know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would the witness make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Sehovac.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: My respects, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please bear in mind that we both have to pause before question and answer so that the interpreters and the court reporters can interpret and record everything. Did you make a statement to the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please let's look at 1D7054 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the statement you see before you now?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that some parts had to be excluded as irrelevant to this case on the order of the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: I am aware that some parts have been excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you read this statement and signed it?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it reflect correctly what you said, and is there anything you would change now?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: It reflects correctly what was said, but there are some typing errors. For example, page 2, point 4, second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the mistake is?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: It says here "SDB." It should be "SNB," because the State Security Service, as you know, was operating before the war, and the SNB was established --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or the SDB, that is, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- was established after that. Another error has occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the transcript -- SDB was before the war; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. And in wartime the SNB was established. And in point 33, the letters have been switched again. It should say here "SDB" and not "SNB." And the same error occurred in point 34: "Did you or the SNB have ..." It should be: "Did you or the SDB have ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sehovac, both of these interventions, does it refer to the questions or to your replies?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: No, I am referring to my responses, because we need to have precise information as to what service was involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: On page 12, point 36(B), the SS tattoo should be deleted. And instead of "Handzar Division" it should say "Young Muslims Unit," and this refers to Mr. Izetbegovic and his past.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the sentence: "Very often the fact was mentioned" --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's it. So that should be deleted. He had an SS tattoo and he was a member of the Handzar Division. No, that's incorrect. He was a member of the Young Muslims Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the tattoo and SS, that should be deleted?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Up to "that he was." And page 36(B), in (B) again the letters say "SDB" instead of "SNB." And I have no further comments to make as regards this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sehovac, if I were to put the same questions to you today, would your answers to them be basically the same as in this statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN SEHOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Basically they would be the same. I would not change anything.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, may I tender this statement and the associated documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll deal with associated exhibits separately. We'll admit the statement first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2852, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To save time, the Chamber has the following questions with respect to 1D921, 1D6133, and 1D6167. I note that there's no English translation have been uploaded. So if they are uploaded now, the Chamber didn't have time to see them, so I would like you to lead live about those ones. And the 1D6147 is included in para 20. That should be redacted. And the Chamber has doubt as to the relevant -- relevance of 1D6132, 1D6134. So in order to tender them, after explaining the relevance to the Chamber, I would like you to lead live as well when the Chamber satisfied with its relevance. And with respect to 6136, which is an intercept, you should lead with the witness how he was able to authenticate that intercept, whether he himself was an intercept operator or otherwise. Mr. Sehovac, we are about to adjourn and continue tomorrow morning, but as you may be already aware, you are not supposed to discuss with anybody else about your testimony. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 31st day of January, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
